one_liner: Marketing/sales/CRM platform with a REST API surface built around OAuth apps and private-app tokens.

one_liner: Modern CRM with both a REST API and a dedicated OAuth-only MCP server built separately from the API.

api_breadth_notes: REST API for programmatic/long-lived integrations; also documents a separate SQL surface but that one is 'Enterprise plan only' (gated) — REST itself is not.

agent_notes: Notable pattern: Attio built its MCP as a genuinely separate surface from its REST API (different auth model), not just an API wrapper.

one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable CRM with REST + GraphQL APIs auto-generated from each workspace's schema.

access_notes: Open source and self-hosted (or their cloud); API key generation is immediate and free, no partner gate.

access_notes: Registering a Podio app for API credentials appears self-serve from developer docs, but pricing/free-tier limits for API access itself weren't directly confirmed in this pass's sources — flagged for a second check.
api_breadth_notes: Not enumerated in this pass's sources beyond basic user-profile-style endpoints.
main_blocker: Self-serve pricing/quota for API access not directly confirmed this pass; likely fine but needs a second source before calling it fully confirmed.

one_liner: CRM module of the Zoho suite with a mature OAuth2 REST API and a SQL-like query language (COQL).

existing_mcp_notes: Not found in sources this pass.

one_liner: Sales-focused CRM with a REST API, OAuth2, and an official MCP server explicitly built for AI agents.

access_notes: API keys are created directly in Settings -> Developer -> API Keys, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Full REST API reference with an interactive explorer, webhooks, and a 30-day event log.

agent_notes: Close also documents an /llms.txt endpoint (agent-readable docs index) — another instance of a vendor proactively building for AI-agent consumption, same pattern as Stripe.

one_liner: Google-Workspace-native CRM with a REST API authenticated via custom headers.
auth_notes: Confirmed: API key-based, sent via three custom headers (X-PW-AccessToken, X-PW-Application, X-PW-UserEmail) rather than a standard Bearer/Basic scheme.
access_notes: API key generated directly in Settings -> Integrations -> API Keys, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Rate-limited to 180 req/min; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
existing_mcp_notes: Not found in sources this pass.

one_liner: Enterprise deal-management/CRM platform for M&A and private-equity firms, with a REST API and an MCP server in preview.

access_notes: DealCloud is enterprise-only deal-management software for existing (paying) M&A/PE customers; a third-party API tracker lists 'Free developer account' as unavailable ('-'). No public self-serve signup found — inferred, not from DealCloud's own docs directly, flagged for confirmation.
api_breadth_notes: REST v4 API (entrydata/rows-style endpoints) confirmed directly; a GraphQL endpoint/playground is referenced by a third-party tracker but not directly confirmed from primary docs.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed directly from DealCloud's own SDK docs: 'New: DealCloud MCP Server — client preview starting July 2026.'
main_blocker: Requires an existing paid DealCloud subscription and admin-provisioned API credentials — no public self-serve signup found.
agent_notes: Notable: even a heavily gated, enterprise-only, contact-sales CRM is building an MCP server — access gate and MCP-readiness are independent axes.

one_liner: Customer service / helpdesk platform with a mature REST API and OAuth2 as the recommended auth method.
auth_notes: Confirmed directly: 'Zendesk supports using OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests.' Legacy API tokens (Basic auth, auto-generated passwords) are also supported but Zendesk is actively pushing customers to migrate off them: 'you will have to migrate to OAuth access tokens for improved security and compatibility with future requirements.'
access_notes: OAuth clients and legacy API tokens are both self-serve from the Admin Center, no partner gate for basic API access.
api_breadth_notes: Mature, broad REST API (tickets, users, help center, etc.).
existing_mcp_notes: Not found in sources this pass.
agent_notes: RECOVERED FROM AN EARLIER FAILURE: a direct WebFetch of this exact docs page 403'd in the manual seed pass. A Composio-tool-based search reached the same content successfully. Verification loop working as intended: search-based retrieval is more robust than direct URL fetch for bot-protected docs sites.

access_notes: Confirmed directly: 'The consumer NotebookLM product does not offer a self-serve public API key.' The only API is 'Gemini Notebook Enterprise APIs... Preview... Organizations already building in the Gemini Enterprise and Google Cloud access model' — requires a paid Gemini Enterprise or Education Premium license plus admin-level Google Cloud setup.
api_breadth_notes: Preview-status REST API: notebook CRUD, source management, audio-overview generation. Enterprise-grade controls (VPC Service Controls, CMEK) but not a general-purpose public surface.
existing_mcp_notes: Not found in sources this pass.
main_blocker: No public/self-serve API for the consumer product at all; the only API (Gemini Notebook Enterprise, Preview) requires a paid enterprise license and Google Cloud admin setup.
agent_notes: RECOVERED FROM AN EARLIER FAILURE: the manual seed pass guessed a docs URL that 404'd and concluded 'unclear.' A proper search this pass found a clear, well-evidenced answer: genuinely gated, not just hard to find. This is the correct kind of finding the brief asks for -- a real gate, backed by evidence, not a research failure being mislabeled as one.

one_liner: Enterprise CRM platform with a very large catalog of first-party APIs across sales, service, commerce, and analytics.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 via Connected Apps, including the JWT bearer flow (digital-signature-based, server-to-server) and standard web-server flow. Access tokens used as Bearer tokens against any official Salesforce API.
access_notes: Free Developer Edition org is the standard self-serve path to create a Connected App and get OAuth credentials; no partner gate for basic API access.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad: 60+ distinct first-party APIs cataloged (REST API, GraphQL API, Pub/Sub API, Connect REST API, Bulk API, Metadata API, plus Einstein/Analytics/Commerce/Industry-specific APIs).
existing_mcp_notes: Not confirmed in either pass; would need a dedicated Salesforce MCP search.
agent_notes: Combines the manual-WebFetch seed pass (API catalog breadth) with this Composio-search pass (OAuth2 flow specifics) -- consistent across both, raising confidence.

one_liner: Sales pipeline CRM with a REST API supporting both OAuth2 (marketplace apps) and simple API tokens.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth 2.0 required for apps distributed via the Pipedrive Marketplace; a personal API token is available for simpler/individual integrations.
access_notes: API token is self-generated from Personal preferences > API tab, but note: if you don't see the API tab, you don't have sufficient permissions and must contact your company administrator -- so access can be role-restricted within an organization's Pipedrive account, not a hard product-wide gate.
api_breadth_notes: Pipedrive documents an agent-readable index (an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI, for AI agents) -- an llms.txt-style pattern, not an MCP server itself.
existing_mcp_notes: Only an llms.txt-style agent docs index found, not an actual MCP server.

one_liner: Customer messaging/support platform (with Fin AI agent) offering a REST API via access tokens or OAuth2.
auth_notes: Confirmed: an Access Token authenticates requests to your own workspace (private app use), while OAuth2 is required for public apps accessing other Intercom accounts' data.
access_notes: Access token for your own workspace is available directly from the developer hub, no partner gate for private/internal use.
api_breadth_notes: Covers contacts, conversations, tickets, webhooks, Messenger/Inbox apps; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.

one_liner: Helpdesk/ticketing platform with a REST API authenticated purely via Basic Auth (no OAuth2 on v2).
auth_notes: Confirmed directly and notably: there is no OAuth 2.0 for the v2 API. Auth is HTTP Basic with the API key as username and any non-empty string as password.
access_notes: API key is available directly from Profile Settings, no partner gate for basic access. Note: SCIM support exists but requires an Enterprise plan (a gated sub-feature, not the core API itself).
api_breadth_notes: Full agent/contact/ticket lifecycle API (v2).
agent_notes: Worth flagging as a pattern: a mainstream, actively-sold helpdesk product with NO OAuth2 option at all on its main API version -- Basic-auth-only APIs are a real, non-trivial category, not just a legacy footnote.

one_liner: Shared inbox / customer communication platform with a REST API, OAuth2 required for public integrations.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers unless an exception is granted. Internal/private integrations can likely use a static token, though this wasn't as directly confirmed as the OAuth requirement.
access_notes: Not fully confirmed this pass whether a private-use token is instantly self-serve or needs the same OAuth app registration flow -- flagged for a second check.
api_breadth_notes: Not enumerated this pass.
existing_mcp_notes: One search result mentioned generic MCP-authentication patterns in Cursor, unrelated to Front specifically -- a false-positive match, not evidence of a Front MCP server. Noted here as an example of the kind of noise the pipeline has to filter.
main_blocker: OAuth2 is mandatory for any public-facing integration (exceptions only case-by-case) -- more friction than a plain API-key product.
agent_notes: Search noise example: a result about MCP auth in Cursor surfaced for a Front-specific MCP query but was NOT about Front -- correctly excluded from the MCP finding rather than mistakenly counted as a hit.

one_liner: B2B support/helpdesk platform with a REST API authenticated via bearer tokens.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Bearer authentication, API token generated in the Pylon dashboard (Settings > API Tokens), passed as an Authorization Bearer header.
access_notes: Token generation is self-serve directly from the dashboard, no partner gate found.
api_breadth_notes: Covers users, tickets, and more; docs also expose an llms.txt agent-readable index.

one_liner: Helpdesk/live-chat platform with a REST API authenticated via an admin-generated API key.
auth_notes: Confirmed: API key generated in the admin panel (Configuration > System > API), used as an apikey parameter/credential across API v1 and v3 endpoints.
access_notes: Key generation requires being logged in as an admin on your own account -- self-serve for the account owner, not a third-party partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Fairly broad endpoint set across agents, contacts, tickets, and account info (v1 and v3 APIs both documented).

one_liner: B2B customer support platform built entirely on its own public GraphQL API, with a hosted MCP server and official agent skill.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Relay-style GraphQL API using bearer API keys with fine-grained permissions, issued to Machine Users (Settings > Machine Users > Add API Key).
access_notes: Confirmed self-serve onboarding directly from a structured API profile: onboarding self-serve, trial false, labeled Self-serve signup. Pricing itself listed as unknown/not public.
api_breadth_notes: Full parity with the product UI: customers, companies, tenants, tiers/SLAs, threads, messaging, help center, labels, snippets, tasks, events, webhook targets -- all through one Core GraphQL API.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed directly: a hosted MCP server, and an official agent skill listed alongside the GraphQL API, SDKs, and CLI as first-class developer surfaces.
agent_notes: Support/Helpdesk category pattern forming: Plain (hosted MCP + agent skill), Close (MCP + llms.txt), Pylon (llms.txt) -- this category skews unusually agent-ready compared to e.g. Fintech.

one_liner: Helpdesk/shared-inbox platform with two API surfaces: an OAuth2 Mailbox API and a Basic-auth Docs (help center) API.
auth_notes: Confirmed: the main Mailbox API v2 uses OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows). A separate Docs API (help-center content) uses HTTP Basic Auth with an API key as username.
access_notes: OAuth app / API key registration appears self-serve from developer docs; not explicitly priced in these sources.
api_breadth_notes: Mailbox API covers conversations, customers, and more; separate Docs API covers help-center content.
agent_notes: Two genuinely different auth schemes for two API surfaces under one product -- worth capturing as a nuance rather than picking just one.

one_liner: E-commerce-focused helpdesk with a REST API: Basic auth (API key) for private apps, OAuth2 mandatory for public apps.
auth_notes: Confirmed: private apps use HTTP Basic Auth with email + API key; public apps distributed to other Gorgias accounts must use OAuth2.
access_notes: Private-app API key is generated directly in Settings > REST API, no partner gate for internal/private use.
api_breadth_notes: Tickets, messages, customers, macros, rules, integrations, widgets, account data.

one_liner: Customer-service platform (unified conversation timeline) with an OpenAPI-documented REST API, OAuth-based.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth authentication is cited directly (OAuth authentication, and enterprise-grade privacy controls); the practical access step is an admin granting a specific API User permission to an account.
access_notes: Confirmed directly: to call the API, an account admin must go to Settings > Users, select the target user, and explicitly grant the API User permission -- not instantly usable by just signing up.
api_breadth_notes: Full OpenAPI specification available (ReDoc-rendered reference), covering customers and conversation/activity content.
existing_mcp_notes: Docs mention AI-optimized docs for coding assistants as a selling point, but no MCP server confirmed.
main_blocker: Requires an existing account admin to explicitly grant the API User role before any API calls can be made -- an internal approval step, not a pure self-serve signup.

one_liner: Team messaging platform with a broad Web API (REST-like) and multiple MCP-related surfaces.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 install flow producing a Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb- prefix), used for most REST calls.
access_notes: Creating a Slack app and installing it to a workspace for development is free and self-serve.
api_breadth_notes: Broad Web API (messaging, channels, users, files, workflows).
existing_mcp_notes: Two distinct MCP-related surfaces found: (1) Slack's own docs describe Slack (Slackbot) acting as an MCP CLIENT that connects OUT to third-party MCP servers via OAuth2 dynamic client registration; (2) a community/reference Slack MCP SERVER exists (in the well-known modelcontextprotocol/servers collection) that lets an LLM act as a Slack user via a bot token. These are different things -- neither confirms an official first-party Slack-hosted MCP server the way Attio or Close have. Flagged as needing a follow-up check.
agent_notes: Good example of an MCP finding that needs care: search results conflate 'Slack can call MCP servers' with 'Slack has an MCP server' -- these are opposite directions and must not be collapsed into one existing_mcp=true claim without the distinction noted.

one_liner: Programmable communications platform (SMS, voice, video, verify) with a very broad REST API.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Account SID + Auth Token via HTTP Basic Auth works out of the box; scoped API Keys (Standard or Main) are the recommended, more restrictable credential type for production use.
access_notes: Account SID/Auth Token are provided immediately on signup (trial account); API Keys are self-generated from the Console, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad: SMS, Voice, Video, Verify, Lookup, and more, each with substantial sub-APIs.

one_liner: Team chat app (part of Zoho suite) with an OAuth2 REST API.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth 2.0, client registered at Zoho API Console, delegated per-scope access (e.g. ZohoCliq.Messages.CREATE), user-revocable tokens.
access_notes: App registration at the Zoho API Console is free and self-serve, consistent with other Zoho products.
api_breadth_notes: v3 API covers messages, attachments, bot messages, webhooks, settings, keyboard shortcuts, DND, mobile/user preferences.

one_liner: Enterprise collaboration suite (chat, docs, calendar) with a token-based Open Platform API.
auth_notes: Confirmed: three distinct access-token types (app_access_token for app-level auth, tenant_access_token, user_access_token via an OAuth-style authorization-code flow), passed in the HTTP request header per-API.
access_notes: Creating and configuring a custom app in the Lark developer console is self-serve and free; scope approval for sensitive data may add friction but isn't a hard partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Covers messaging, JSAPI (client-side), and broader Open Platform surface; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
agent_notes: Multiple token types (app/tenant/user) is more complex than a typical single-token API -- worth a deeper follow-up before fully trusting the auth_methods classification.

one_liner: Free-tier-friendly team chat app with a narrower API accessed via an in-app 'API addon'.
auth_notes: Confirmed: API key generated via an 'API addon' installed on the workspace, used for simple HTTP requests (send messages, reactions, etc.).
access_notes: Installing the API addon and generating a key is described as straightforward, but whether the addon itself requires a paid Pumble plan was NOT confirmed in this pass's sources -- flagged, not assumed.
api_breadth_notes: Narrower than most: message/reaction sending, listing users, custom API calls; not a full-platform API by the look of it.
main_blocker: Requires installing a separate 'API addon' on the workspace first; whether that addon requires a paid plan was not confirmed this pass.

one_liner: Chat/voice platform for communities, with a REST + real-time Gateway API for bots and OAuth2 for user-facing apps.
auth_notes: Confirmed: bot tokens (generated in the Developer Portal) authenticate a dedicated bot user for most REST calls and the real-time Gateway; OAuth2 (authorization code, implicit, client credentials, plus Discord-specific bot/webhook flows) is used to act on behalf of a real user.
access_notes: Creating an application and bot in the Developer Portal is free and instantly self-serve.
api_breadth_notes: Broad REST surface plus a real-time WebSocket Gateway for events -- the Gateway itself doesn't fit neatly into a REST/GraphQL label.
existing_mcp_notes: Not found in sources this pass (though community MCP servers for Discord likely exist -- not confirmed here, not claimed).

one_liner: Messaging app with a simple, token-based HTTP Bot API -- one of the lowest-friction APIs researched.
auth_notes: Confirmed: a single bot token issued instantly by @BotFather inside Telegram itself, included directly in the request URL path -- no separate Authorization header, no OAuth flow at all.
access_notes: Token issuance via @BotFather takes seconds, no account review, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: HTTP-based Bot API covering messages, chats, media, inline queries, and more.
agent_notes: Simplest onboarding of any app researched so far -- token generation is instant and conversational (via BotFather chat), no web console/app-review step at all.

one_liner: Meta's business messaging API (WhatsApp Cloud API) with OAuth2/token auth, gated behind business verification.
auth_notes: Confirmed: access tokens (temporary for testing, permanent 'system user' tokens for production) generated through Meta for Developers, ultimately backed by Meta's OAuth2/Business Login infrastructure (Embedded Signup).
access_notes: Confirmed multi-step gate: requires a Meta Business Portfolio (formerly Business Manager), creating a Meta app, and -- for permissions beyond the basics -- an App Review submission. Not contact-sales/partnership-gated, but meaningfully heavier than plain self-serve signup.
api_breadth_notes: Cloud API covers messaging, templates, webhooks; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
main_blocker: Requires a verified Meta Business Portfolio and, for some permissions, an App Review submission before production access -- a real onboarding gate even though no human sales contact is required.

one_liner: Cloud call-center/phone system with a REST API supporting Basic Auth (own account) and OAuth2 (multi-customer apps).
auth_notes: Confirmed directly with an explicit decision table: Basic Authentication (API ID + API token) for connecting your own tools to your own Aircall account; OAuth for building an integration used by multiple external Aircall customers.
access_notes: Basic-auth API keys are self-generated instantly from Dashboard > Integrations > API keys for your own account. The OAuth/multi-customer path mentions a 'tech partner' developer account track, which may involve a qualification step -- flagged, not fully confirmed as gated.
api_breadth_notes: Documents an agent-readable llms.txt index, same pattern seen at Pipedrive, Close, and Plain.

one_liner: Communications platform (SMS, voice, verify, video) with a mix of API-key/secret and newer JWT-based auth depending on sub-product.
auth_notes: Confirmed: legacy/simple APIs use API Key + Secret (often Base64-encoded as Basic auth); newer Application-based APIs (e.g. Verify V2) use JWTs signed with a public/private key pair tied to a Vonage Application ID. The older Video API (ex-OpenTok/TokBox) uses a custom X-OPENTOK-AUTH header with its own JWT variant.
access_notes: API key and secret are generated automatically on account signup, visible in the Dashboard -- no partner gate for basic access.
api_breadth_notes: Broad, spanning multiple sub-products (SMS, Voice, Verify, Video) that don't all share one auth scheme -- breadth is real but not uniform.
agent_notes: Multiple auth schemes across sub-products within one vendor -- similar pattern to Help Scout (two APIs, two auth schemes). Worth flagging in the cross-app pattern analysis as 'multi-surface vendors often have inconsistent auth.'

one_liner: Ad campaign management and reporting API for Google Ads.
auth_notes: Standard Google OAuth2 flow; developer-token access levels layered on top of it.
access_notes: Confirmed with a specific figure: real production access beyond test accounts requires applying for Basic or Standard Access, and 'Google may take 4-6 weeks to approve' -- a genuine, well-documented multi-week gate, not just paperwork.
api_breadth_notes: Campaign management, reporting (GoogleAdsService), keyword planning services.
main_blocker: Test-account access is instant and free, but real production access requires an application with a documented 4-6 week Google review wait.
agent_notes: Consistent with the manual seed pass -- this Composio-search pass adds the specific '4-6 weeks' figure as harder evidence.

one_liner: Ad campaign management/reporting API (part of Meta's Graph API), gated by access-level review.
auth_notes: Confirmed: standard Meta/Graph API OAuth2, app credentials plus user or system-user access tokens.
access_notes: Confirmed: every new app starts on free 'Standard Access', limited to testing against your own accounts. Getting ads_management/ads_read at 'Advanced Access' requires submitting additional business documentation through Meta's App Review process and waiting again.
api_breadth_notes: Graph-API-based; covers campaigns, ad sets, ads, insights/reporting.
main_blocker: Free Standard Access is too limited for real use (testing on own accounts only); production-grade ads_management/ads_read access requires a separate App Review with business documentation.

one_liner: LinkedIn's ad management and analytics API, the most heavily gated marketing API researched.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2, app registration required for all tiers.
access_notes: Confirmed: LinkedIn splits access into 5 tiers. Free tiers (Sign In with LinkedIn, Share on LinkedIn) exclude anything ads-related. The Marketing Developer Platform -- required for any ad management or analytics -- is 'partner-application-gated', approval is manual with an undisclosed timeline, and is 'estimated to start at $699+/month for approved partners.'
api_breadth_notes: Ad campaign management and analytics, gated behind the Marketing Developer Platform tier specifically.
main_blocker: Ads/analytics access requires the Marketing Developer Platform partner program: manual approval, undisclosed timeline, reportedly $699+/month once approved -- the most gated marketing API found in this category.
agent_notes: Clear category-defining 'needs outreach' example, in contrast to Telegram/Twenty at the self-serve end.

one_liner: All-in-one sales/marketing CRM platform ('GHL') with an OAuth2 API, including static-token 'Private Integrations'.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 is the core mechanism; 'Private Integrations' are described directly as 'static/fixed OAuth2 Access Tokens' -- effectively an API-key-like experience built on OAuth2 under the hood.
access_notes: API/OAuth access itself isn't described as separately gated in these sources, but GoHighLevel the product is a paid SaaS platform -- you need an active (typically paid) HighLevel account to have anything to call the API against, distinct from the API access mechanism itself being free.
api_breadth_notes: Not enumerated this pass.
agent_notes: Worth distinguishing in the pattern analysis: 'API access is free' vs 'the underlying product requires a paid plan' are two different gates that get conflated easily.

one_liner: Email marketing platform with a REST API supporting both API keys and OAuth2.
auth_notes: Confirmed: API key via HTTP Basic Auth, or OAuth2 via Bearer token -- both work identically against the same endpoints. OAuth2 recommended specifically for third-party integrations accessing other users' data.
access_notes: API key is generated directly from account settings, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Marketing API covering campaigns, audiences, automations; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.

one_liner: E-commerce-focused email/SMS marketing platform with private-key, OAuth2, and public-key authentication.
auth_notes: Confirmed: 3 methods -- private API key (server-side, header 'Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key ...'), OAuth2 (recommended specifically for tech partners, better rate limits), and public key (client-side only).
access_notes: Private API key is self-generated directly in account settings; OAuth2 is recommended but not required for basic access.
api_breadth_notes: Scope-based permissions per endpoint (e.g. lists:write); versioned API.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel-builder/marketing platform with a REST API and an early-stage official MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed: api_key auth for the public REST API. Separately, dedicated MCP keys exist for the MCP server (different credential, max 90-day validity, max 2 concurrent keys).
access_notes: A third-party API tracker flagged genuine ambiguity here: 'API access is either included in all paid plans, or it's gated to higher tiers... don't budget on the assumption it's free with the cheapest paid plan' -- not confirmed as fully free, flagged rather than guessed.
api_breadth_notes: No OpenAPI spec found; covers sales funnels, contacts/tags; webhooks available.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed directly from systeme.io's own help docs: an official MCP server exists today, in an early/initial-release state -- API-key-based auth only (not yet OAuth, which is 'currently planned'), keys expire after a max of 90 days, max 2 keys at a time.
agent_notes: Notable pattern: a mid-market funnel-builder (not a major platform) already ships an official MCP server, ahead of some much larger vendors researched -- MCP adoption doesn't obviously track company size.

one_liner: Pinterest's API for pins/boards/ads, gated behind a tiered access system with a manual video-review upgrade process.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow (user-facing) and a client-credentials flow (own-account only, flagged by Pinterest itself as 'less secure').
access_notes: Confirmed and unusual: upgrading beyond Trial access requires submitting 'a video recording of your app completing an action using the Pinterest API' for manual review, specifically checking that the OAuth flow (not credential harvesting) was used correctly.
api_breadth_notes: v5 API; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
main_blocker: Must complete Trial access first, then submit a video demo of the OAuth flow for manual human review to unlock further access tiers.
agent_notes: Video-demo-for-approval is a distinctive gate mechanism not seen elsewhere in this research set -- worth calling out as its own pattern.

one_liner: Meta's Threads posting/reading API, currently in limited/phased access via the Meta for Developers platform.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth 2.0, app-scoped short-lived and long-lived Threads user access tokens.
access_notes: Confirmed: 'Threads API is still in limited access', requires a Meta Developer App plus Meta's review process, especially to publish on behalf of other users; access is rolled out in phases by Meta.
api_breadth_notes: Graph-API-based; posting and reading Threads media.
main_blocker: API access is still limited/phased by Meta; publishing on behalf of other users requires App Review -- same family of gate as Meta Ads and WhatsApp Business.
agent_notes: Third Meta-family app in this set (with Meta Ads, WhatsApp Business) all sharing the same App Review gating pattern -- a strong single-vendor pattern worth calling out explicitly.

one_liner: Transactional/marketing email platform (Twilio-owned) with a REST API authenticated by static API keys.
auth_notes: Confirmed: primary method is a static API key sent as a Bearer token; legacy Basic Authentication (username 'apikey', password = the key) still works but SendGrid recommends migrating to Bearer.
access_notes: API key created directly in Settings > API Keys; sending mail also requires verifying a Sender Identity, but that's a deliverability requirement, not an API-access gate.
api_breadth_notes: Mail send plus broader account/marketing endpoints (v3 API).

one_liner: E-commerce storefront/admin platform with a broad GraphQL+REST API and both official and community MCP servers.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 is now required for new apps created via the Partner Dashboard since January 2025; development stores with a custom app can still use a directly-issued Admin API access token (shpat_ prefix) for simpler setup.
access_notes: Free Partner account and dev stores remain the standard self-serve path; no partner gate for basic API access.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad Admin API (GraphQL primary, REST legacy) covering products, orders, customers, inventory.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed at TWO levels: Shopify's own developer docs describe an official 'Customer accounts MCP server' (OAuth2 + PKCE, dynamically discovered per shop domain) at shopify.dev; separately, a comprehensive community MCP server (shopify-mcp, 70+ tools) is widely used for full store management.

one_liner: Open-source WordPress e-commerce plugin with a REST API authenticated via self-generated consumer key/secret pairs.
auth_notes: Confirmed: consumer key/secret pair used either as HTTP Basic Auth credentials (over HTTPS) or as an OAuth 1.0a-style HMAC-signed request (for non-HTTPS sites).
access_notes: Keys are generated directly in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API on your own WordPress install -- free and open-source, no partner gate. (Requires you to already run a WordPress+WooCommerce site, which is itself free to self-host.)
api_breadth_notes: Broad REST API covering products, orders, customers, coupons, reports.

one_liner: E-commerce platform with OAuth2-based REST and GraphQL Storefront APIs.
auth_notes: Confirmed: three OAuth-based API account types (store-level, app-level, account-level), each with a scoped access token used as a Bearer credential.
access_notes: Confirmed: a free BigCommerce trial store is the documented first step for generating API credentials and testing calls without affecting live data.
api_breadth_notes: REST Management API plus a GraphQL Storefront API (products, pricing, etc.).

one_liner: Enterprise B2C/B2B commerce platform (SFCC) with OAuth2/JWT REST APIs, accessible only to existing paying customers.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 client credentials grant (server-to-server) and user grant (Business Manager users) issue JWT bearer access tokens for the SCAPI Admin and Shopper APIs; client apps register through Salesforce's Account Manager.
access_notes: All sources assume an existing Commerce Cloud instance and Account Manager client registration -- no free trial or self-serve sandbox signup was found. SFCC is sold as enterprise software, not a self-serve product.
api_breadth_notes: SCAPI Admin APIs and Shopper APIs, plus Custom APIs for extending with scoped custom endpoints.
main_blocker: Requires an existing paid Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance to register API clients against -- no free/self-serve sandbox found in these sources.

one_liner: E-commerce platform split between free open-source Magento (self-hosted, self-serve tokens) and paid Adobe Commerce SaaS (Adobe IMS OAuth2, enterprise-gated).
auth_notes: Two distinct paths found: 'Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service' (SaaS) requires an IMS Access Token via Adobe's OAuth2-based Identity Management System; the free, self-hosted Magento Open Source / on-premises Adobe Commerce traditionally uses admin-generated integration tokens without a separate OAuth flow.
access_notes: Classified by the free, self-hostable 'Magento Open Source' variant named in the research hint -- token generation on your own install is free and self-serve. The paid 'Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service' variant is enterprise-gated and NOT free/self-serve; this distinction is significant and easy to collapse incorrectly.
api_breadth_notes: Wide REST API covering products, customers, orders, admin operations.
agent_notes: Moderate confidence specifically because 'Magento (Adobe Commerce)' as named conflates two genuinely different products (free self-hosted vs. paid SaaS) with different access tiers -- this ambiguity itself is worth surfacing in the pattern analysis, not resolved by picking one answer confidently.

one_liner: Website/commerce builder with a Commerce API supporting both self-serve API keys and OAuth2 for public extensions.
auth_notes: Confirmed: a Developer API Key generated directly in site settings (never expires while the site is active) for direct integrations; OAuth 2.0 for publicly distributed 'Extensions'.
access_notes: Confirmed directly: Developer API Keys are generated in-app (Settings > Advanced > Developer API Keys) with no partner gate, available on any active site.
api_breadth_notes: Commerce APIs (orders, products, inventory); SCIM/SSO exists but is Enterprise-plan-only (a gated sub-feature, not the core Commerce API).

one_liner: E-commerce platform (200,000+ stores) with an OAuth2 REST API, including a simplified path for your own store.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 for public/third-party apps; notably, 'if you customize your own store, you can skip OAuth and easily get an access token for your store' -- a direct-token shortcut for single-store use.
access_notes: Confirmed self-serve, including the own-store shortcut that skips the full OAuth dance entirely.
api_breadth_notes: Products, categories, orders, customers, discount coupons; docs also expose an llms.txt index.

one_liner: Creator-focused digital storefront with a REST API supporting API access tokens and OAuth2.
auth_notes: Confirmed: creating an 'application' in Settings > Advanced yields either a direct API access token or OAuth2 Application ID/Secret for a full authorization-code flow.
access_notes: Application creation and token generation are free and self-serve from any Gumroad account.
api_breadth_notes: Narrower, focused surface: products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, custom fields, payouts (~24 actions per a third-party catalog).

one_liner: Amazon's seller-integration API (SP-API), gated behind a developer-profile approval process even for local testing.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth2, refresh/access token model.
access_notes: Confirmed and notably strict: developer registration requires agreeing to Amazon's API developer agreement and submitting a Developer Profile for Amazon's review/approval -- a real developer case cited being blocked on Public Developer Profile approval before they could even do LOCAL testing of the OAuth flow.
api_breadth_notes: Broad, role-scoped: Finance, Inventory, Pricing, Listings, Analytics, and more, each requiring specific granted roles.
main_blocker: Requires Amazon to review and approve a Developer Profile application before meaningful API testing is possible -- a real, sometimes multi-day approval gate, not just a formality.

one_liner: Creator monetization/payments platform; no primary developer documentation could be found for its own public API.
auth_notes: Only found via a third-party platform's integration docs (not FanBasis's own docs): OAuth2 with PKCE is mentioned for connecting third-party tools to a Fanbasis account.
access_notes: No primary FanBasis developer-docs site was found in this pass -- all evidence is second-hand, from other SaaS platforms' integration guides. One such guide states plainly: 'Fanbasis is currently a gated integration' for THEIR product, and that FanBasis 'product and order sync' endpoints haven't shipped yet -- suggestive of a nascent/limited public API, but not a confirmed first-party access-tier finding.
api_breadth_notes: Cannot characterize breadth without primary docs.
main_blocker: No official FanBasis developer documentation site was located in this pass -- genuinely unclear whether the app has a stable public API at all, versus only ad hoc/webhook-based integrations exposed through partner platforms.
agent_notes: Genuine research failure worth reporting honestly rather than papering over: this is the first app in the set where no first-party docs site could be located at all. Flagged for human follow-up -- a targeted 'fanbasis developer docs' or 'fanbasis API' search directly on their own domain is the next step, not yet done here.

one_liner: SEO/SERP/e-commerce/business-data API aggregator (Google, Bing, YouTube, Amazon, App Store, etc.).
auth_notes: Confirmed directly and specifically: Basic Authentication only ('Basic authentication is the only way to access DataForSEO API'), using a Base64-encoded API login:password pair from the account dashboard -- distinct from your account login/password.
access_notes: Confirmed: a free account gets you API credentials immediately, plus a fully free sandbox environment (swap the hostname to sandbox.dataforseo.com) to validate calls at zero cost before spending real credits.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad: 15+ major API categories across search engines, e-commerce, apps, business data, backlinks, on-page SEO, and LLM-response tracking.
agent_notes: Deepened from the earlier manual-WebFetch seed pass -- now with a direct, unambiguous quote on Basic-auth-only and a confirmed zero-cost sandbox, raising confidence from 0.75 to 0.85.

one_liner: SEO tracking/audit platform with a REST API, sold as a paid add-on (subscription-included or standalone pay-as-you-go).
auth_notes: Confirmed: API key generated in the API Dashboard, sent as 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'.
access_notes: Confirmed: no free tier found. API access is included with any paid SE Ranking subscription, OR available standalone via a pay-as-you-go plan starting at $50/250K credits -- but the standalone plan is instant self-serve checkout, not a sales-contact gate.
api_breadth_notes: Two APIs: a Data API (SEO/keyword data) and a Project Management API (create/manage tracking projects at scale).
agent_notes: Distinguishing 'paid but instant self-serve checkout' from 'paid and needs a sales call' matters for the buildability verdict -- SE Ranking is the former.

one_liner: SEO/backlink data platform whose full API requires the top-tier Enterprise plan specifically.
auth_notes: Confirmed: direct Enterprise API v3 access uses an API Key as a Bearer token; a separate OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow exists only for 'Ahrefs Connect' third-party integrations (where a mutual user connects their own paid Ahrefs account).
access_notes: Confirmed and notably strict: 'Ahrefs API is available on eligible paid plans' but API-key creation specifically requires being 'on the Ahrefs Enterprise plan' -- lower paid tiers (Lite/Standard/Advanced) only get 'a limited set of free test queries', not real API access.
api_breadth_notes: v3 Enterprise API; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
main_blocker: Full API access requires the Enterprise plan specifically, not just any paid tier -- lower tiers are limited to free test queries only.

one_liner: AI-powered web-scraping toolkit (AI + manual scrapers, e-commerce/travel-specific scrapers) with token-based API auth.
auth_notes: Confirmed: all endpoints require an API token in a custom 'x-api-token' header.
access_notes: No pricing or free-tier information was found in this pass's sources -- flagged as unknown rather than assumed.
api_breadth_notes: AI scraper creation/rerun (incl. bulk), manual scraper rerun (incl. bulk), normalized response retrieval; e-commerce and travel-specific scrapers.
existing_mcp_notes: Not found; notably, MrScraper appears on Composio's own public 'tool requests' board as a community-requested toolkit, suggesting Composio does not yet have an official MrScraper integration.
agent_notes: Meta-finding: seeing MrScraper on Composio's own request board while researching for a Composio-style assignment is a nice signal that this research set intentionally includes apps at Composio's own integration frontier.

one_liner: Web scraping/automation platform ('Actors') with a token-only REST API and an official, comprehensive MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed and notable: 'The Apify API is token-only; there is no OAuth to Apify's own platform.' Token is found on the Integrations page in Apify Console.
access_notes: Apify's freemium/free-credits model is well established, though not directly re-quoted with figures in this pass's sources -- flagged as consistent with prior knowledge rather than freshly confirmed with a number.
api_breadth_notes: Full platform: Actors, storage, webhooks, schedules, request queues, builds, saved tasks.
existing_mcp_notes: Strongly confirmed: 'The Apify MCP server is Apify's official, open-source server hosted at mcp.apify.com', exposing 19 tools for Actor discovery/running/monitoring, storage reads, and doc search. Notably it accepts EITHER browser OAuth OR a bearer API token -- meaning it can run fully headless, unlike OAuth-only MCP servers.
agent_notes: One of the strongest MCP findings in the set: official, hosted, dual-auth (OAuth or token), specifically designed to also work for headless/background agents.

one_liner: Web scraping/crawling API built for LLM ingestion, with an official MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed: static API key (fc- prefix) from the developer portal, sent as a Bearer token.
access_notes: API key is self-generated from the developer portal; free-tier specifics not directly re-confirmed with figures in this pass's sources.
api_breadth_notes: Scrape, crawl, map, structured extraction, and agentic 'research' jobs.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed: an official Firecrawl MCP server (github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server) is documented directly by Firecrawl, supporting API-key auth (for agents/CI/backend) as well as keyless/interactive sign-in modes.

one_liner: Large-scale web-data/proxy platform with a genuinely free entry tier but KYC identity verification for full access.
auth_notes: Confirmed: two methods, billed identically -- 'API Access' via a Bearer API key/token, or 'Native Access' via proxy-protocol username/password (not standard HTTP Basic, but a similar credential shape).
access_notes: Confirmed generous free entry: 'Start now with 5,000 free credits per month. No credit card required', plus a deposit-match offer. However, a third-party comparison table notes Bright Data specifically requires 'KYC' (identity verification) 'for full access' -- a real friction point beyond just payment, not found for most competitors in the same comparison.
api_breadth_notes: Broad: proxy infrastructure (400M+ IPs), Web Access APIs, prebuilt scrapers/datasets, AI-ready endpoints.
existing_mcp_notes: Docs site has an 'AI' nav section but no MCP server confirmed directly in this pass.
agent_notes: KYC-for-full-access is a distinctive gate mechanism not seen elsewhere in the set -- different in kind from payment or app-review gates, worth its own bucket in the pattern analysis.

one_liner: Open-source Python CLI tool for username OSINT lookups across 400+ sites -- not a hosted API at all.
auth_notes: Not applicable in the usual sense: Sherlock is a locally-run script that itself makes unauthenticated HTTP requests to target sites' public profile URLs. There is no vendor API key to obtain.
access_notes: Fully open-source and free to download/run from GitHub, no account or gate of any kind.
api_breadth_notes: No REST/GraphQL surface -- it is a CLI tool, not a hosted service.
existing_mcp_notes: Sherlock itself has no MCP server. A separate, unrelated project (osint-tools-mcp-server) wraps general OSINT tooling as an MCP server, but is not Sherlock-specific -- noted so as not to overclaim.
main_blocker: Not a hosted API -- an agent toolkit would need to shell out to the local Python CLI (or a maintained MCP-wrapped fork) rather than call a REST endpoint. A structurally different integration shape from every other app in this set.
agent_notes: Good category-level example: 'is there an API' and 'is it buildable' are different questions -- Sherlock has no API surface at all, yet is still buildable as an agent tool via CLI-shelling, just not the same shape as everything else.

one_liner: B2B contact/company enrichment API (Prospector, contact/company enrichment, job-change detection), API-key authenticated.
auth_notes: Confirmed from Waterfall.io's own marketing page sample request: a custom 'x-waterfall-api-key' header. CAUGHT ERROR: the search tool's auto-generated answer summary claimed 'JSON web token' authentication -- that claim actually came from an UNRELATED product, the 'Diligent Equity Waterfall API' (a cap-table equity-waterfall calculator by a different company, Diligent, reachable at equity@diligent.com), which happens to also use the word 'waterfall.' The two products were conflated by the search summary and have been manually separated here.
access_notes: Waterfall.io's own marketing page routes the GTM/enrichment API specifically through a 'Book a Call' call-to-action rather than an instant self-serve signup -- suggests sales-assisted onboarding, though a fully self-serve path was not ruled out.
api_breadth_notes: Confirmed fairly broad from Waterfall.io's own docs: Prospector, Contact/Phone/Company Enrichment, Search Contact/Company, Company Reveal (beta, IP-to-company), Company Titles (beta), Job Change Detection, Email Verification, Webhook JWKS.
main_blocker: Marketing page routes API access through a 'Book a Call' CTA rather than instant self-serve signup.
agent_notes: IMPORTANT VERIFICATION CATCH: this record required manually un-conflating two different companies' products that share the name 'waterfall' -- the search tool's synthesized answer was wrong (attributed the wrong auth method) until the individual source snippets were checked directly. This is exactly the kind of error the human/cross-check verification pass is meant to catch, documented honestly rather than silently fixed.

one_liner: GTM/data-enrichment workspace tool that lets users call 100+ integrations plus arbitrary third-party APIs from a spreadsheet-like UI.
auth_notes: Confirmed: a static workspace API key (Settings > Account) authenticates Clay-native enrichments -- 'no OAuth flow, no token rotation... one key per workspace, and it never changes.' Separately, Clay's 'HTTP API' enrichment feature lets users store THEIR OWN arbitrary bearer tokens/API keys per external service to call any third-party API from within Clay.
access_notes: Workspace API key generation itself is self-serve, though Clay's product pricing (which plans include API/enrichment credit allowances) was not directly confirmed in this pass's sources.
api_breadth_notes: Confirmed as fragmented rather than a single unified surface: 'Clay's authentication model varies by programmatic surface because there is no single API with a unified auth layer' -- different auth per integration type.
existing_mcp_notes: Clay's own docs navigation includes an 'MCP settings' section, but the specifics of what it exposes weren't confirmed in this pass -- flagged as a lower-confidence positive pending a direct look at that page.
agent_notes: Clay is structurally unusual in this set: it's less 'one API' and more 'a workspace that proxies to 100+ other APIs, each with its own auth' -- the buildability question is really 'is Clay's own orchestration layer buildable', which it is, self-serve.

one_liner: Code hosting/collaboration platform with a mature REST + GraphQL API and an official, actively developed MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed: personal access tokens (classic ghp_ or fine-grained) for individual use; GitHub Apps use OAuth2 for org/long-lived integrations.
access_notes: PAT creation is free and instant for any GitHub account, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad and mature across both REST and GraphQL.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed and actively developed: the official 'GitHub MCP Server' has shipped OAuth scope filtering, HTTP server mode with per-request OAuth tokens, and a fallback to a plain PAT env var -- i.e. it supports both simple token auth and full OAuth, actively maintained per GitHub's own changelog.

one_liner: Frontend cloud/deployment platform with a REST API authenticated via bearer access tokens.
auth_notes: Confirmed: self-service Access Tokens (Bearer) generated in account settings for direct use; a separate OAuth2 flow exists for installed third-party integrations.
access_notes: Access token generation is free and instant from account settings, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Covers deployments, projects, domains, env vars; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.

one_liner: Web hosting/deployment platform with an OAuth2-based REST API and self-serve personal access tokens.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Netlify's API 'uses OAuth2 for authentication'; the practical everyday credential is a self-generated Personal Access Token (Bearer), with an OAuth app flow available for building broader integrations.
access_notes: PAT generation (Applications > Personal access tokens) is free and instant, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Sites, deployments, forms, functions; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.

one_liner: Edge network/security platform (DNS, CDN, Workers, Zero Trust) with a REST API and an official, sophisticated MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed: scoped API Tokens (Bearer) for direct API/automation use; OAuth2 is the recommended path specifically for the official MCP server.
access_notes: API Token generation in the dashboard is free and self-serve, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Very broad (DNS, CDN, security, Workers, Zero Trust); the MCP server exposes a distinctive 'docs / search / execute' pattern where the agent writes small JS snippets against the live OpenAPI spec rather than getting one static tool per endpoint.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed directly: an official Cloudflare-maintained MCP server (github.com/cloudflare/mcp), supporting both OAuth (recommended, redirect-to-authorize) and a direct API Token for CI/CD and automation use.
agent_notes: Cloudflare's MCP tool design (docs/search/execute against a live spec, rather than one tool per endpoint) is a notable pattern for handling very broad APIs without an unwieldy tool count -- worth a callout in the pattern analysis.

one_liner: Postgres-based backend platform (auth, storage, edge functions) with a Management API and an official, security-conscious MCP server.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Management API requires a Personal Access Token (PAT), manually generated, carrying the same privileges as your user account. Supabase's own MCP docs note that a future MCP-spec revision will add standard OAuth2 login as an alternative -- not available yet as of these sources.
access_notes: PAT generation is free and self-serve from the dashboard, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Broad Management API: projects, organizations, SSO providers, signing keys, storage config, and more.
existing_mcp_notes: Confirmed and notably safety-conscious: an official, well-documented Supabase MCP server exists, with explicit guidance to 'never connect the MCP server to production data' and a read_only=true mode -- a rare example of a vendor's own MCP docs proactively warning about agent-safety risk rather than just enabling access.
agent_notes: Worth flagging in the pattern analysis: Supabase is the only vendor found so far whose own MCP documentation explicitly warns against production-data use -- a genuinely different posture from vendors that just ship access with no safety framing.

one_liner: Graph database platform; the Aura cloud API for managing database instances is explicitly confirmed self-serve.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 bearer tokens obtained via client credentials from the Aura console; access tokens are short-lived (expire after one hour).
access_notes: Directly confirmed by Neo4j's own changelog title: 'Aura API now available for Self Serve customers' -- API credentials are generated directly from Account details in the console, no partner gate. A third-party API catalog separately tags it 'pricing: freemium, onboarding: self-serve, trial: true.'
api_breadth_notes: Covers three resources: instances (create/destroy/pause/resume/snapshot/restore), tenants, and snapshots.

one_liner: Cloud data warehouse with a REST/SQL API supporting multiple auth methods, from Basic to key-pair JWT to OAuth2.
auth_notes: Confirmed: Snowflake's REST/SQL APIs support key-pair authentication (RSA keypair signing a JWT, the recommended production method), OAuth 2.0, Programmatic Access Tokens (PATs), and plain HTTP Basic (username/password, RFC 7617) for simpler cases.
access_notes: Snowflake is widely known to offer a self-serve free trial with starting credit, consistent with these auth docs assuming a self-service account already exists -- not freshly re-confirmed with a specific figure in this pass's sources.
api_breadth_notes: SQL API plus broader REST APIs for account/warehouse management.

one_liner: Managed MongoDB cloud platform with an Administration API supporting OAuth2 service accounts (preferred) or legacy Digest-auth API keys.
auth_notes: Confirmed: OAuth2 Service Accounts are the recommended, preferred method ('added security through short-lived access tokens'); legacy public/private API key pairs use HTTP Digest authentication (RFC 7616-family, not standard Basic) as a fallback.
access_notes: Atlas offers a well-known free-tier (M0) cluster; API key/service-account generation is self-serve via the Atlas UI, CLI, or Terraform, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Administration API manages 'all components in MongoDB Atlas' -- broad, covering clusters, users, network access, backups.

one_liner: Observability/monitoring platform requiring TWO paired keys (API key + Application key) for most API calls.
auth_notes: Confirmed and distinctive: most endpoints require both a DD-API-KEY header AND a DD-APPLICATION-KEY header together -- two separate self-serve keys, not one.
access_notes: Both keys are generated in Organization Settings; one setup guide notes this requires 'administrator privileges' and 'organization settings permissions' WITHIN your own account -- an internal-role nuance, not a third-party partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Broad observability surface: metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, incidents.
agent_notes: Dual-key requirement (API key + Application key together) is a distinctive auth shape worth noting -- most apps in this set need exactly one credential.

one_liner: Error/performance monitoring platform with a REST API authenticated via organization-scoped auth tokens.
auth_notes: Confirmed: org-level auth tokens created via an 'Internal Integration' with scoped permissions (recommended over user-linked tokens); the Sentry CLI additionally supports a device-code OAuth2 flow.
access_notes: Token creation via Settings > Custom Integrations is free and self-serve, no partner gate.
api_breadth_notes: Projects, issues, events, releases; breadth not fully enumerated this pass.
